A1.justification: Both complete, readable 23-page PDFs describe the same work, renamed from SnapMem to 3D-Mem. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices 6-14 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SnapMem evaluations on A-EQA, EM-EQA, and GOAT-Bench, together with appendix ablations and failure-case analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical evaluations under the name 3D-Mem, including benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix 11 retain the same clustering, incremental snapshot updates, prefiltering, VLM navigation, and fine-tuning objectives. The new name and 'multi-view images' wording describe the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same A-EQA, EM-EQA, and GOAT-Bench coverage, including HM3D/ScanNet scenes and category, language, and image navigation goals. Appendix 11 retains the same training-data coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1-5 is unchanged, including Explore-EQA, ConceptGraphs with Frontier Snapshots, caption and Multi-Frame baselines, GOAT-Bench baselines, and the no-memory variant. Renaming SnapMem does not introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain the 184-question A-EQA evaluation, GOAT-Bench's 36 scenes and 278 subtasks, the same metrics and baseline-specific controls, and GPT-4o/LLaVA configurations. Preprocessing, training budgets, and experimental settings in Appendices 9-11 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The no-memory comparison, decision-frequency experiment in Appendix 6.2, failure cases in Figures 5-10, and sensitivity sweeps over observation count, object distance, and prefiltering classes in Figures 13-15 are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without evaluation seed or repeated-run disclosures, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 and the result plots retain the same values and findings. Examples include A-EQA scores of 52.6/42.0, EM-EQA's 57.2 at 3.1 average frames, and GPT-4o GOAT-Bench success/SPL of 69.1/48.9. Appendix breakdowns, ablations, and qualitative outcomes are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The snapshot definitions and coverage constraints in Section 3.1.1, clustering termination argument, frontier formulation, and incremental update equations are unchanged. No mathematical result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both claim compact visual scene memory, explicit exploration through frontier snapshots, and scalable lifelong memory through incremental aggregation and prefiltering. Rephrasing the work as a multi-view 3D scene memory framework preserves these contributions and the benchmark-performance claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving spatial context, retrieval, and persistent memory remain the same. Appendices retain the same qualifications concerning viewpoint matching, VLM perception, detection failures, multi-floor environments, and oscillation between frontiers.

D1.justification: The front-page project address changes from vis-www.cs.umass.edu/snapmem to embodied-agi.cs.umass.edu/3dmem/. Implementation settings, hardware, training details, and complete prompts remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: The same 45 cited works and research positioning are retained. Section 2 and Appendix 13 preserve the comparisons with 3D scene representations, Topological Semantic Graph Memory, and RoboHop.

P1.justification: SnapMem is renamed throughout to 3D-Mem, the title is shortened, and the abstract receives limited rewriting. Several passages replace 'snapshot-based' with 'multi-view images,' and one affiliation changes. Section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The title and author block are reformatted, Table 1 moves from PDF page 7 to page 6, and nearby content reflows. Captions, table labels, and Figure 12's pseudocode identifiers reflect the renaming; existing figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 mainly rebrands and lightly edits v1 while retaining the same method, experimental evidence, appendix analyses, and limitations. The tighter abstract and modest layout adjustments have limited impact; rebranding also leaves the old SnapMem legend in Figure 4. Overall clarity and scientific support remain essentially unchanged.
